title: Literature review: pelvic and abdominal loading tolerance under belt restraint
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. REQ-L3 thresholds are TBD. Automotive lap-belt, aviation and fall-arrest literature covers pelvis and abdomen tolerance, belt migration (seat-belt syndrome) and submarining.
objective: Summarise published injury criteria and test data for pelvis/abdomen loading through a lap or hip belt, including load direction, duration and ATD measures (e.g., THOR abdomen), and note which apply to an upward (−Gz) ejection load path.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 12 peer-reviewed or standards-body sources, each cited
Separates load directions (forward crash vs upward ejection)
Lists candidate thresholds for REQ-L3 as 'candidate, for engineer review', not as requirements
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
